experiments.question: Can a bundled workspace on/off ablation falsely attribute graph-prior and projection effects to workspace selection?
experiments.design: 2x2x2 GRAPH_PRIOR x WORKSPACE_SELECTION x PROJECTION synthetic potential-outcome model; 60 local seeded replications x 5000 items plus independent Judge0 Python replication with 30 x 3000 items.
experiments.interpretation: Bundled ablation can manufacture a large apparent workspace effect even when workspace selection has zero causal effect. Stage-orthogonal interventions recover the constructed direct effect. Numeric magnitudes are toy-specific.
experiments.boundary: synthetic identifiability calibration, not FRANK effect size

experiments.task: 12 deterministic highest-UTILITY selections; GRAPH_PRIOR and WINNER explicitly non-authoritative; A-D preserve candidate order and cross metadata truth; E reverses candidate order; separate neutral order controls remove both metadata fields.
experiments.prior_mesh_replication: Earlier Groq 8B GWT proxy reported 87.5% neutral vs 62.5% reversed-order matched-content accuracy and projection integrity 8/8 correct, 0/8 truth under deliberately scrambled projection.
experiments.interpretation: The model is highly sensitive to projection/order and contextual metadata interactions. The matrix is not a stable estimate of independent GRAPH_PRIOR or WINNER effects; it is evidence that naive winner lesions are confounded unless order/format/content are fixed or counterbalanced. Pure order control changed accuracy by 16.7 percentage points in this small sample, directionally matching the earlier 25-point proxy gap.
experiments.boundary: hosted 8B proxy only; no Qwen3-4B or live FRANK claim
